findings.surface: Cross-cutting IAM condition evaluation / shared evaluator + 8 cross-service policy validators
findings.claim: The single root cause is: services/common/src/iam_authorization.rs reads a Condition clause whose key the request NEITHER carries in Request::context NOR declares in Request::published as UNDECIDED (None), and collect_applying reads None fail-closed in BOTH directions (an Allow grants nothing, a Deny still refuses). Because no cross-service validator derives aws:SecureTransport from the actual transport, the AWS-recommended `Deny` with `Bool: {aws:SecureTransport: "false"}` is applied to HTTPS/TLS requests. Five separately filed GH issue families (#369, #409, #447, #451, #459) plus an SES receipt-rule report are this one defect.
findings.root_cause: iam_authorization.rs:1400-1525 conditions_hold(): `[] if modelled => absence_holds || is_negated(operator)` (1493) only fires for a PUBLISHED key; every other absent key takes `_ => { required.note(...); decidable = false; continue; }` (1494-1498), so `decidable.then_some(held)` returns None (1524). collect_applying (1219-1225) maps `None if allows => continue` and lets a Deny fall through into `into.push((denies, ...))`. Per-service validators construct Request::new(...).with_context(...) with only aws:SourceArn/aws:SourceAccount (or no context at all) and never publish aws:SecureTransport; AWS always puts that key in the request context and would evaluate the Bool clause as false on TLS, so the Deny does not apply.

findings.surface: Root-cause diagnosis correction / DynamoDB resource policies + KMS key-policy lockout check
findings.claim: GH #459's title/hypothesis ('aws:SecureTransport is false for HTTPS requests') is WRONG against HEAD source. The key is not given the value 'false'; it is absent from the request context and undeclared as a published key, so the Bool clause is UNDECIDED and the fail-closed reading keeps the Deny. This matters for the fix: setting the key to 'true' in one place is insufficient while the evaluator still refuses on undecided clauses.
findings.root_cause: DynamoDB's condition_context() enumerates only dynamodb:LeadingKeys/Attributes/Select/EnclosingOperation plus principal tags, federated claims and aws:PrincipalType; published_condition_keys() publishes that same set. KMS's request_conditions() publishes SourceArn, SourceAccount, PrincipalArn, PrincipalAccount, the encryption-context family and kms:ViaService; neither contains aws:SecureTransport. An unmodelled key therefore never reaches clause_holds(), and conditions_hold() returns None.

findings.surface: Bool / BoolIfExists / StringEqualsIfExists / negated conditions / Null on an unmodelled key
findings.claim: The shared evaluator implements IAM's IfExists suffix and negated-operator absent-key rule ONLY for keys the caller declares in Request::published. On an UNPUBLISHED key, `StringEqualsIfExists`, `BoolIfExists` and negated operators are left UNDECIDED instead of evaluating the condition element as TRUE, so an Allow never grants and a Deny still refuses - a divergence from AWS's documented absent-key rule. The repository's own unit test asserts this behavior explicitly.
findings.root_cause: conditions_hold():1443 computes `modelled = publishes(request, key)`; :1493 `[] if modelled => absence_holds || is_negated(operator)`; :1494-1498 everything else sets decidable=false. split_if_exists (:1605-1609) strips the suffix but cannot rescue an unmodelled key. is_negated (:1615-1617) is a substring heuristic `operator.contains("Not")`. Null is likewise decidable only for a published key (:1452-1468), and `NullIfExists` is treated as no operator at all (:1423-1426).
evidence: services/common/src/iam_authorization.rs:280-290 (IF_EXISTS_SUFFIX doc quoting AWS: 'if the key is not present, evaluate the condition element as true'), :286-289 ('Absence is only decidable for a key the request DECLARES it models ... for every other key the clause stays undecided')
